minutes.headline: Facilities director presented the FY2024 capital requests; the committee asked questions and voted on no capital items.
minutes.summary: The Capital Planning Committee heard the new facilities director walk through completed and pending projects and next year's priorities, including Brooks House repairs, public safety building roof and the Eagle House parking lot. Members questioned maintenance backlog, unspent appropriations for HVAC condensers and a drainage study, and the placeholder cost of the parking lot. They approved prior minutes by roll call, planned the prioritization process and set the next meetings, then adjourned.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee voted on no capital items; it heard the new facilities director present the FY2024 capital requests.
The facilities director reviewed the status of approved FY2022-23 projects, then FY2024 priorities including Brooks House, the public safety building roof and the Eagle House parking lot.
Members questioned an earlier drainage study appropriation that now seems unnecessary, and whether Eagle House condenser funds will cover the work.
A member questioned the placeholder cost of the Eagle House parking lot, which had no design or space count; the director will send detail once the engineer finishes.
The committee agreed a process of public discussion, individual ratings tallied, then a final discussion, and set the next meetings for November 9 and November 21.

why_it_matters: These requests feed the capital list that goes to town meeting, so the ratings and the final list set which building projects residents are asked to fund through taxes.
Placeholder costs for the parking lot, the Brooks House move and the roof are not yet backed by designs or bids, so the amounts residents eventually see may differ from these.
